evidence_kinds.decision_and_effect: the witness case has at least one decision finding and at least one effect finding
evidence_kinds.effect: the witness case has effect findings only; no decision differs from the oracle
evidence_kinds.missing_evidence: the witness case is UNASSESSABLE through missing terminal evidence; no finding is claimed. The barrier timeouts this causes are not exempt as a class: each is predeclared by case and step in run_exceptions

technical_failures: A patch that does not apply, changes another file than its target, or fails the SUT typecheck or build, a case inventory other than the control's, a harness process error, an uncaught exception or a crash of the gate is a technical failure (exit 2) and never a detection. Each whole mutant run is checked before it is classified: every harness error (any case) and every barrier timeout must be exactly one predeclared in the mutant's run_exceptions, case by case; any other is a technical failure, and a predeclared one that does not occur is no detection.

evidence_parts.containment: an unexpected start, commit or delivery, or a side effect after the terminal: something ran that must not
evidence_parts.lifecycle: an unexpected approval_granted or permit_issued: lifecycle state that must not exist; never containment
evidence_parts.availability: a missing start, commit, delivery, approval or permit: an allowed action that did not happen
evidence_parts.signal: cancellation and revocation acknowledgements and premature or unexpected terminals
evidence_parts.check_point: decision findings without any effect finding
evidence_parts.missing_evidence: no finding; UNASSESSABLE through missing evidence

masking: A masked mutant changes a check that no case can reach under the pinned runtime mode. Its whole run is pinned to equal the control (exit, every case, diagnostics); it is a recorded gap, never a detection, and a run that differs is a technical failure.

not_run.plan_row: approval-permit lifecycle plan section 8.1, M25: over-fencing control, the issue state check requires pending instead of approved; witness approval-before-cut step 1 (false_deny@1, missing_permit_issued@1); kind check and lifecycle
not_run.reason: The plan patch also changes the setup: every authority that starts issued is created through process(), approve() and issuePermit() (plan section 7.2, D2), and its setup issue is then denied (not_approved). Every case with such an authority fails its setup (setup_failed, a harness process error that is never predeclarable), so the whole mutant run is a technical failure, never a detection. Replacing the patch with another over-fencing mutant deviates from the approved plan and is left to a decision; nothing replaces it here.
not_run.reproduction: Precheck of mutations/revocation/M25-issue-requires-pending-over-fencing.patch against ef775db (node dist precheck, same path as the gate): approval-before-cut shows false_deny@1, false_deny@2, missing_permit_issued@1, missing_execution_started@2, missing_tool_commit@3, missing_output_delivery@4, but 19 corpus and 9 supplement cases report setup_failed ("setup approve and issue of a's lineage failed: Lifecycle issue denied: not_approved [lineage-1]") and HARNESS_ERROR identity_mapping_invalid (no setup baseline probe). The patch file is kept for the reproduction and is not part of the gate.
not_run.coverage_gap: The issue state requirement (issue only from approved) has no eval mutant evidence: no mutant of it can be run without breaking the lifecycle setup, and the setup is never switched off for a mutant. M25-overreach is a separate mechanism (over-reach of a session revocation at issue) and is not evidence of this property. The requirement itself is still observed (for example, the issue of a lineage that was never approved is denied in pending-approval at step 2, and the runtime-own test L10 asserts not_approved), but no eval mutant shows that the gate would detect its loss.
